recommendations.rationale: The retained-but-unread backend-motion channels (tension_tracking_error_n, force_limit_saturated, tendon_length_m/rate, optimization_nonconverged, usability and feasibility-recovery flags) are the records that could support or exclude the actuation/limit family within the sampled 0.01-0.35 s coverage; reading them is a derived-view read and requires no numerical work, backend execution or parameter change.

Completing coverage of source.one_step_predictions, source.plan_selection, source.solver_status, source.applied_tensions and source.controller_horizon for the unread update ids would test whether horizon reduction, solver-status patterns and commanded-input divergence coincide with the late-window speed excursion, but it cannot establish dominance on its own.
Testing planner/solver degradation requires the warm plans and iteration traces that are not retained; obtaining them is prerequisite and cannot be satisfied by any tool available in this run.

Recorded weights such as terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0 do not by themselves demonstrate that the tip-speed term was inactive or decisive, and a single execution with an unreplayed trace does not justify a parameter edit; any configuration change is out of scope for this phase.

The retained inventory states no closed-loop counterfactual or full-backend-replay capability, so the divergence between terminal reach and the failed settling window can be bounded observationally (position criterion met, speed criterion exceeded in the late and terminal samples) but no dominant cause can be adopted.

attribution.reason: Reach acceptance gates position error against 0.01 m and the recorded terminal error 0.007642608585867386 m satisfies it, whereas the settling criteria additionally gate tip speed against 0.02 m/s over a 0.05 s window; the recorded terminal speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s and late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810152739742807 m/s both exceed 0.02 m/s. This accounts for how the two verdicts can differ (speed criterion unmet while position criterion met); it is an observation-level reconciliation and does not identify why speed remained high.

The retained per-update GVS projection residual is small at update 0 (0.0 rad/m) and rises monotonically over sampled updates to 2.500592461937906 rad/m at update 28, i.e. projected GVS state divergence from the backend grows in the sampled coverage. Sampled one-step predicted and measured next errors stay close, so this supports growing projection/model divergence but does not establish that mismatch dominated the settling failure; dominance would require the full backend replay that the inventory states is unavailable.

mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 against control_period_s 0.01 and 35 deadline misses, with 34 User_Requested_Stop versus one Solve_Succeeded, document a wall-time overrun of the recorded per-update budget. Scope note: the run record states synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so the overrun by itself does not explain the simulated late-window speed/position behaviour.

The recorded scheduling semantics (synchronous controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps; wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time) excludes physical delay injection from the recorded wall-time overrun as an explanation of the late-window speed drift.

Retained per-update fields show the effective horizon reduced from the configured 10 to 7 at update 28 and raw solver statuses returning User_Requested_Stop with policy reasons budget_best_feasible (early) and relative_seed_improvement (late), but optimizer iteration traces and full warm plans are not retained (control_snapshots.json, full_snapshots_available false) and the backend-motion channels optimization_nonconverged, unusable_updates, feasibility_recovery and plan_source were not displayed in the reads performed; degradation therefore cannot be established or ranked from retained evidence.

Sampled aligned intervals show applied tensions identical to the commanded constant vector with applied_input_difference_n 0.0 at update 0, but the last sampled updates command markedly different vectors with near-zero components (update 34 component 1.4216485070827969e-08 N). The retained channels tension_tracking_error_n and force_limit_saturated exist in source.backend_motion but were not read in this context, so neither tracking error nor saturation-driven settling failure is supported or excluded.

Within the sampled aligned intervals (updates 0-25) the applied-tension vector is constant with largest component 4.755852667139922 N, and the inventory records per-tendon force limits of 8.0 N for all six tendons in source.force_limits; no tendon in those sampled intervals is at its recorded limit. This scopes only the sampled intervals and the sampled channels and does not cover unread force_limit_saturated indications.

The recorded configuration carries terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0 with tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02, terminal_weight 5.0, velocity_weight 0.0001 and numerical_source 'bundled_guess', which is consistent with a planner that does not drive the recorded terminal/late tip speed toward the 0.02 m/s settling limit while the late speed is 1.5810152739742807 m/s. Because raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without recorded contributions or scaling, and because holding-phase weights are not present in the current fact catalog, this remains a consistency observation rather than a supported cause.

facts.statement: The same summary reports reach achieved and settling failed: reach_passed true with reach_tolerance_m 0.01 and terminal_error_m 0.007642608585867386, while sampled_settling_passed is false under criteria position_limit_m 0.01, speed_limit_m_s 0.02, window_s 0.05, with late_max_error_m 0.05813810428573256 and late_max_speed_m_s 1.5810152739742807; the recorded terminal_speed_m_s 0.6351726092425104 also exceeds the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

Recorded per-update GVS projection residual magnitude grows over the sampled updates (0.0 rad/m at update 0, 0.15722764549262314 at update 4, 1.4319114299302802 at update 16, 2.1832800954411686 at update 24, 2.500592461937906 at update 28), while sampled one-step predicted next errors remain close to measured next errors (0.05092697997271693 vs start_error_m 0.051323589596878036 at update 0; 0.03935705993481866 vs actual_next_error_m 0.04425206792540656 at update 20).

Recorded mean update wall time is 17.075238151415917 s against control_period_s 0.01, with deadline_misses 35 and stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop 34 / Solve_Succeeded 1; configured recipe horizon is 10 control intervals, while recorded per-update effective_horizon is 10 at updates 0 and 4 and 7 at update 28.

Recorded recipe entries relevant to tip speed include terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02, terminal_weight 5.0, velocity_weight 0.0001, and numerical_source 'bundled_guess'; raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions or scaling.

limitations: Single execution (execution_id 5991de53e82747439e87ba8569667e1b); model comparisons and one run do not establish a dominant cause.

Only two evidence reading turns were used, covering update_ids 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28 (prediction), 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29 (prediction), 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28 and 2, 6, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34 (plans), plus the derived motion view's final window 0.30-0.35 s; the remaining update subsets were not read.

Frame difference respected: world-frame tip vectors (aligned interval positions/velocities/errors), projected GVS coordinates for saved states and controller-side predictions (rad/m, rad/(m*s)), and serial backend joint coordinates for motion; no cross-frame numerical combination was performed.
No numerical work was performed: no local solves, prediction evaluations, integration, backend solves, workers, saved-state grants, check selection/execution, or configuration changes.
Historical optimizer iterations and full warm plans are not reconstructed (control_snapshots.json not retained; full_snapshots_available false).

Closed-loop counterfactual replay, continuous-time reconstruction and full backend replay are not computable with the current tools; the derived motion view displays the final settling window only, and the raw backend-motion container is gzip bytes not readable as JSON.
recommended_actions: Defer any conclusion about the actuation/limit family until the unread retained channels (tension_tracking_error_n, force_limit_saturated, tendon_length_m/rate, per-sample deadline flags) in source.backend_motion are read for the sampled range.

Defer any ranking of planner/solver degradation until the unread subsets of source.one_step_predictions, source.plan_selection, source.solver_status and source.controller_horizon (updates 3, 7, 10, 11, 14, 15, 18, 19, 22, 23, 26, 27) are read and the not-retained control_snapshots.json iteration traces are obtained.

Defer any configuration change (e.g. tip-speed-related weights or scales) pending evidence of actual cost-term contributions; a single execution with recorded weights cannot justify a parameter edit, and no configuration change is in scope here.

Defer any claim of a dominant cause: no closed-loop counterfactual replay or full backend replay capability exists in the inventory, so remaining alternatives can only be narrowed, not resolved, with retained records.
